<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par156 />&c.;<ref>The expression {{GHGheb|text=הִתְרָאָה פָנִים|translate=to look one another in the face}} (i.e. to contend in combat) {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=14|verse=8}}, 11, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=25|verse=17}}, 21, is probably only a shortened form for {{GHGheb|text=הִתְרָאָה פָנִים אֶל־פָּנִים}}.</ref> so also ''to cast oneself down'', {{GHGheb|text=אַפַּ֫יִם אָֽרְצָה|translate=the face}} being turned ''to the earth'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=1}}, &c. (for {{GHGheb|text=אָֽרְצָה}} we find {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=23}}).<ref>That {{GHGheb|text=(אֶ֫רֶץ) אָֽרְצָה}} is really to be regarded as a virtual predicate to {{GHGheb|text=אַפַּ֫יִם}}, and not {{GHGheb|text=אַפַּ֫יִם}} as a ''casus instrumenti'', is seen from {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=23}}, where {{GHGheb|text=אַפַּ֫יִם אֶ֫רֶץ}} precedes the verb.</ref>—Cf. finally the formula {{GHGheb|text=אֵם עַל־בָּנִים|translate=mother with children}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=12}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=14}} and {{GHGpar|119|aa}} note 2.

Rem. On circumlocutions of this kind to express negative attributes by means of short noun-clauses (complete or incomplete), cf. {{GHGpar|152|u}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|156|d}}
'''3.''' As circumstantial {{GHGterm|verbal}}-clauses,<ref>Some examples of these have been already discussed in another connexion above, {{GHGpar|120|a}}–c.</ref> we find (1) sometimes affirmative clauses (see below), but far more frequently (2) negative clauses (see f), and among these (3) a certain number of expressions which may be regarded simply as equivalent to negative adverbial ideas (see g).

Examples of (1) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=11}}<sup> ''b''</sup> woe unto them, that tarry late in the evening, {{GHGheb|text=יַ֫יִן יַדְלִיקֵם|translate=while wine inflames them}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=31|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=7|verse=26}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=20|verse=15|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=4|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=21|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=62|verse=5|hidebook=1}}. The circumstantial verbal-clause is used to particularize an action which has before been expressed generally, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=48|verse=14|hidebook=1}}=''crossing his hands''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=19}}; antithetically, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=כִּחֵשׁ לוֹ|translate=wherewith however he lied unto him}}. The verbal-clause seems to assign a reason in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=מִשְׁפָּט צִוִּ֫יתָ|translate=since thou hast commanded judgement}}; a consequence in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=103|verse=5}}.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=14}} the circumstantial verbal-clause {{GHGheb|text=שָׂם עַל־שִׁכְמָהּ}} is only due to a harmonizing transposition; read {{GHGheb|text=וְאֶת־הַיֶּ֫לֶד שׂ׳ ע׳ שׁ׳}}. According to the source used in cap. 21 Ishmael was still a young child; according to 17:25 he was about 16 or 17 years old.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|156|e}}
Rem. On the cases in which an imperfect in the sense of a final clause is subordinated to a verb of motion (generally {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}}), see {{GHGpar|120|c}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|156|f}}
Of (2), subordinate verbal-clauses with {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} (in English usually rendered by ''without'' and the gerund, if the subject be the same as in the principal clause), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=1|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא יַבְדִּיל|translate=without dividing}} it ''asunder''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=34}}; {{GHGheb|text=לֹא}} with the perfect is so used in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=44|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=34|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=30|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=26}} (''without its being blown upon it''). With a different subject, equivalent to a consecutive clause in English, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹֽא־יָקֻ֫מוּ|translate=so that they shall rise up no more}}.—Moreover, verbal-clauses in the same sense (''without'' doing, &c.) are frequently connected by {{GHGheb|text=וְלֹא}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=42|verse=3|hidebook=1}}; in a concessive sense, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=44|verse=18}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|156|g}}
Of (3), cf. {{GHGheb|text=לֹא יֵדַע}} (prop. ''he knows it not'') ''unawares'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=35|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא יַחְמֹל|translate=unsparingly}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=14}} (after an infinitive absolute); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hb|chapter=1|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=10}} (but {{GHGheb|text=וְלֹא יַחְמֹל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=22|hidebook=1}}; see f at the end); {{GHGheb|text=לֹא כִחֵ֑דוּ}} (prop.
